The Operator is what I would describe as a psychological spy/detective thriller where you investigate crimes. Quite honestly, what you see on the store is what you get. The atmosphere (early-mid 1990s) is fantastic and does a great job immersing you into the world. The story is very good (albeit a bit short) so I won't go into much detail about it. That said, the moment(s) of realization actually did surprise me more than I expected, especially later on in the story (I'm sure fellow players remember their experience realizing the thing about [spoiler]THAT camera feed[/spoiler]).

For the game itself, I enjoyed many aspects of it but was somewhat let down by others. The core gameplay loop is quite fun, and it doesn't impede on the storytelling. The largest "disappointment" - also a common theme in fellow reviews - the game is just too darn short. I felt like I went a bit slow, and my playthrough lasted about 3.5 hours. Given the cheap price I felt like it was a good deal, but I think extending it it to maybe 6 hours would make the rising action and climax much more appreciated. The puzzles, while somewhat challenging, varied and engaging, were generally one-trick ponies that I expected to use at least one or two more times during the game.

Would I recommend this game? Yes. Despite it being shorter than I expected, I still feel like I paid a good price for a well-written thriller story that I could tell had a lot of love put into it. I'm hoping the devs make another game like this that's more meaty with the game content and length, I would definitely purchase it.

reviews.review:
Really enjoyed this! I've read some criticisms about the length and the ending, but for me both of those were perfect. It's nice to play a complete game in a few hours sometimes.

The mystery and puzzle solving aspects were pitched well and kept me guessing throughout and it hit all the right 90s X-Files buttons.

It took me about 3 hours to complete, but I didn't feel it was too short or long. Some people are unhappy that it ends on a sort of downer cliffhanger ending, but to me it was the perfect ending for a story of faceless government conspiracies. The ending hints at a continuation anyway, and I'm up for that.

My only real criticism is that I didn't really like the blurry cutscenes. I understand the aesthetic choice for those, but I just felt they were too long overall, when they should have just been short transitions from one scene to another.
Good story with some good twists

This feels like a demo. The puzzles are very simple and short and most of the game is listening or reading dialogue. The puzzles are mostly "click on the person's face" or "navigate the floor plan", not really anything where you need to connect knowledge or have an idea. Ending feels rushed and pointless. Not really worth the price tag, but I hope the developer can iterate on this formula and make a longer and better game in the future.
reviews.developer_response: Hello, thanks so much for playing our game. We appreciate it. I'm sorry that the experience left you wanting more. We really hope to make a game that is longer and more complicated in the future. We would have loved to explore more ideas in The Operator but, unfortunately, didn't have the budget. Hopefully, we can do so on our next project. Thanks again for playing.

reviews.review:
I don't write many reviews and this one is more of a warning in some ways. 

This is much more of a click along adventure with a couple of mini games. I haven't replayed the game to see if the solutions to the mini games are random or fixed. But i purchased the game after playing the demo and that definitely felt like the game would involve much more gameplay and hard work, perhaps some red herrings and a chance to fail.

It is hard to give a proper review of the game without ruining it for people, but it is very short. The slow delivery of text communications or waiting on videos to play pads it out considerably at times and it does feel deliberate to lengthen the game especially at times when there is tension and i personally felt i would be doing things much faster if i had been allowed.

Now don't take that the wrong way, i suspect most people who complain it is short were wanting more. Even if you work out the twists before they come it is worth getting to the end, though it does feel a bit disappointing when you already worked out the big reveals early on. And yes if you look carefully you will at least suspect very early in the game what some outcomes will be. 

Over all the game concept and execution is good, i would have preferred more puzzles or having to dig a bit more for solutions to problems, you are given tools you use exactly once and then never have to use again. It feels set up for a sequel and i hope that they do make one with a longer story.

If you are looking for a click along movie and enjoy that type of game then it may be worth full price to you.
If you are looking for a complex puzzle game where you are the one solving things wait till it is on sale but still get it.
